annotations.title: Set how the site goes live

description: Record how a publish reaches the live site, after the developer's OWN host has been wired. Tusk never touches the host itself and never stores host credentials: it only remembers the deploy hook URL so a future client Publish can trigger a rebuild. Typical flow for a git-linked host: in the host (e.g. Cloudflare Pages → Settings → Deploy Hooks) create a deploy hook, ensure the build runs `tusk pull` with TUSK_TOKEN, then call this with `deployHook` (the URL the host issued) and `deployMode: "hook"`. Use `deployMode: "feed"` instead if the site pulls updates itself with no hook. `deployHook` must be an https URL, or vercel://token@team/project for a Vercel project with no git link. Replaces any hook already set.

deployHook.description: The deploy hook URL the host issued (https, or vercel://token@team/project). Omit in feed mode.

deployMode.description: "hook" (default): a publish pings the deploy hook to rebuild. "feed": the site pulls updates itself, no hook — this also turns on the token-less public feed at <TUSK_URL>/api/public/<slug>/snapshot (CORS open, so the live page can fetch it from the browser). Publish once to start it; until the first publish it serves no pages.

domain.description: The live hostname, if not already set.

previewUrl.description: An https address Tusk can reach to scan/preview and to check the site is live.
